tagline: Up the old Boston to Concord stage road.
intro: From the Massachusetts line at Atkinson, NH 121 runs northwest through Hampstead and Chester to Auburn and Massabesic Lake, on the line of a stage road more than 200 years old that ran from Boston to Concord. Between them lie woodland, villages and farmsteads.

At Hampstead the Robert Frost Byway joins from Derry, and the two make one byway of 43 miles. Auburn, at the far end, was called Chester Woods and then Long Meadow before it took its name from Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village.

moments.title: Atkinson
moments.text: Atkinson Academy was founded for boys in 1787 and took girls from 1791, and the building it put up in 1803, after a fire, is still part of the school.

moments.title: Chester Village Cemetery
moments.text: Along Route 121 runs the Revolutionary Quarter of this 1751 burying ground, its stones mostly slate or sandstone, and the cemetery is unusual for how many markers were signed by their carvers.

moments.title: Massabesic Lake
moments.text: The lake whose Abenaki name means at the great water is Manchester's drinking supply, so it is left to sailing, fishing and kayaks, with no swimming.
